column8: Fri 20 Nov: 3a pedigree (idea 2): Graham's five-times coverage as one quantity; the ten covered once in the zero-interest test with the 0.5% margin and the bill fund's fee charged, nothing spare (NUMBERS 2). Fix: five of the ten rest on iBond fund shares paying net asset value, so never the Treasuries she owns for all ten; say Treasuries and Treasury fund shares.

Fri 20 Nov: 3c, Graham's own licence for a thin room when the payer is sure; closes store Q59-040's open point at source. Fix: the top rests on the late-2032 fund, whose payout is its net asset value and not a predetermined amount (IBTM prospectus), so say she is sure of what its Treasury holdings pay and the 0.5% covers the fund's costs, never that she is sure of what the fund pays.

Fri 20 Nov: store; Graham's Table 11-1 shows the multiple rising with unsteady income, and the plan's version runs from full value to nothing; his admission that the tests are arbitrary is a clause at most for 3a.
Fri 20 Nov: presentation note for WORDS, not report text: Graham chose one plain name per quantity, as WORDS keeps the margin (0.5%) apart from the room under the top; footnote end not seen.

Fri 20 Nov: 3a, Graham and Dodd's steadiness rule taken to its limit (income that cannot vary may be consumed in full) explains nothing spare; Keel's extension, labelled so, true only for holdings kept to their dates.

Fri 20 Nov: 3a pedigree with a point: measured under depression rather than prosperity is the zero-interest test, and no high coupon makes up for deficient safety is IPS l.11; never the reason the first plan was dropped (CANON A3).

Fri 20 Nov: 3b, bond selection as a negative art fits capped promises, with Graham's share rules kept for her flexibility. Fix: $28,682 rests mostly on VT grown at the 7.5% forecast, so say it only with if shares earn the 7.5% assumed, or drop the figure; never a plan figure.

Fri 20 Nov: 3a, the 1929 utility buyers' clear-cut prediction is the bet a ladder sized on reinvesting at forward rates makes; more often than not for starts since 1981 is NUMBERS 2's wording; the extra Treasuries remove the prediction.

Fri 20 Nov: 3e, Graham's exceptional margin so the holder never decides under doubt, reached here by a bound. Fix: the judges found IPS l.17's two exits are not both outside Laura's control (a missed deposit can be her own act), so never call both of them events when the plan cannot be carried out.

Fri 20 Nov: 3c, the margin depends on the price paid; the rule fixes the cut and lets the stated figure move with the day's price (4.65% at forwards, 7.24% if bought 3 points higher, NUMBERS 3); one clause.

Fri 20 Nov: 3e (idea 6, aha): Graham's margin absorbs miscalculation; the plan instead counts what it cannot value at nothing and keeps margins only for measured costs; VT at zero still leaves the bottom (NUMBERS 4).
Fri 20 Nov: store; diversification as the margin's companion, used only in VT, where the plan allows itself to be wrong (TNA l.23); pedigree only.

Fri 20 Nov: 3c, the 0.5% passes Graham's three tests (figures about 0.27%, a written cost list, five ended funds within 0.066% of their last price, NUMBERS 0); five funds is a thin record, so no probability, as the row says.
Fri 20 Nov: 3c note, the engine leans to understatement (4.25% coupons against IBTM's 3.50%, each end rounded down, NUMBERS 3); never borrow Graham's adjective for the range rule (WORDS).

Fri 20 Nov: WORDS note, Penn Central shows one ratio on two bases, so each figure carries its basis once. Fix: 6.12% is at forward rates, the rates implied by today's prices, never at the interest the market expects.

Fri 20 Nov: 3c (idea 1, the card's best): Buffett refused a 3.6% margin, yet Laura's 2.32% room is 8.6 times the frictions measured (NUMBERS 8u, Keel arithmetic): wide against its error. Fix: $117,731 is the zero-interest value of what the late-2032 fund pays on its two purchases, fund shares paying net asset value, never a sum of Treasury payments she owns; compare margin with error, never margin with margin.
Fri 20 Nov: store; Rankine's three kinds of factor: a factor means nothing until both its quantities are named, as WORDS names the top's basis.

Fri 20 Nov: 3b, dead load (the ten) against live load (the building), carried in a separate pot. Fix: the 1-in-20 two-year joint rise of 28% needs $32,191, $3,509 more than her flexibility plus anything above the top (NUMBERS 8u, 8q), never about her whole flexibility (label corrected Thu 19 Nov).

Fri 20 Nov: store; Rankine's real against apparent factor: the rule reckons on the worst case, so its room can be small. Fix: 6.12% is at forward rates, the rates implied by today's prices, never the interest the market expects.
Fri 20 Nov: 3c note; Rankine trusts direct measurement over tables, as each end is measured on the trade day from the holdings bought (NUMBERS 0); Quebec (Q193-032) does the same job more vividly.

Fri 20 Nov: 3a, the 1986 switch to factoring both loads and resistance; the plan's bounds came from no probability, so certain rests on bounds and only the 0.5% is calibrated; Bjorhovde abstract only.

Fri 20 Nov: 3a (idea 3): each source of money has its own factor (Treasury payments at 1.00 like steel, iBond fund flows less 0.5%, waiting cash and VT at nothing), which answers why nothing is spare; one clause in plain words.

Fri 20 Nov: 3c, measurement buys a smaller margin (EN 1992 2.4.2.4): the range carries 0.5% because each end is measured on the trade day; the move would buy less than a top stated a year early (NUMBERS 4).

Fri 20 Nov: 3a (idea 3, the card's best): after the factors, a margin of safety of zero passes at NASA, so nothing spare in the zero-interest test is a pass, not a thin plan; say NASA's margin of safety, since the margin in WORDS is the 0.5% alone; the handbook line is from additive-manufacturing guidance.

Fri 20 Nov: 3e, the aircraft 1.5 never covered modelling error; the plan removes the model where it cannot be trusted (interest at nothing, VT at zero for the bottom); NASA slides, the 1934 handbook not read.

Fri 20 Nov: 3a, every safeguard has a price: the zero-interest standard costs the floor $13,565 against Mon 9 Nov's call and $15,000 at each end (NUMBERS 2, 4). Fix: never call the zero-interest standard a margin (WORDS: the margin is the 0.5% alone).
Fri 20 Nov: 3e and Table 3 row 4 (idea 4): a large multiple against bursting said nothing about fatigue; each margin covers one named thing, so the plan lists what none covers (NUMBERS 8u).
Fri 20 Nov: 3c note; a test passed on a specimen the design does not use proves little; the range rule was tested on holdings it does not assume and the par stand-in was dropped (NUMBERS 3).

Fri 20 Nov: store; small repeated fees as fatigue, now charged by name from the trade day (NUMBERS 0, 3); whether the fee correction is told is the lead's call under standing order 22, which amends 21.
Fri 20 Nov: store; Comet scatter as the five ended funds' spread in costs; an early end is a different event (Q193-031); five funds is a small sample.

Fri 20 Nov: 3e and Table 3 row 4, the plan's uncovered event: an early end of the late-2032 fund after the move leaves the top $4,589 short at zero interest and nothing short at today's market rates (NUMBERS 3); restates the register, the Comet frame is the new part.

Fri 20 Nov: 3c (idea 5): a thin margin fails on an estimated load; Laura's holds because each end is computed from the holdings bought, on the trade day, and nothing is stated before it is owned (IPS l.15); the 18%-30% via a secondary only.
Fri 20 Nov: 3e, the Commission's outside the range of experience is why the 0.5% (a record of five funds) is a margin while 16 years of interest gets a bound; read in extract.

Fri 20 Nov: 3a reasoning: Mon 9 Nov's 3-point margin over a forecast was short in 35 of 585 windows and $22,192 at zero interest, and the bound costs $15,000 at each end (NUMBERS 2); whether 3f may tell it is governed by standing order 22, which amends 21.

Fri 20 Nov: 3e lineage for the three verbs (breaks is deep; lowered or shrinks is shallow, NUMBERS 8u); Bernstein measures in real terms, the promises are in dollars; the book itself not read (Carlson's quotations).

Fri 20 Nov: 3e (idea 2): the Great Depression is shallow on Bernstein's 30-year real clock and deep on a payment date; the wording is Financial Planning's summary, so find Bernstein's own words before quoting.

Fri 20 Nov: 3e area (4): Bernstein sorts money by distance, and the case's not adjusted for inflation (l.90) makes the plan sort it by unit; the unit point is store H6-154 and H2-021, the contrast with Bernstein is the new part.
Fri 20 Nov: 3e checklist for area (4) and the audit of the payments; inflation the likeliest deep risk; his odds are for a lifetime investor.
Fri 20 Nov: store; Bernstein's remedies, the deflation cure conflicting (bonds 2013, gold 2015); TIPS only as his remedy and as banned (CANON A14); gold already refused (H9-105).
Fri 20 Nov: 3e (idea 2): behaviour turns shallow into deep; a payment date sells at that day's price with no panic needed, so no promise rests on a share price (IPS l.11, l.17).

Fri 20 Nov: 3f or 3e, one clause: every miss in the 27 Sep model was settled on 1 Jan 2033, when all ten had to be bought (NUMBERS 8s); the check that priced l.11's step, never the reason the first plan was dropped (CANON A3).

Fri 20 Nov: 3c clause: the move is the plan's one scheduled sale of shares, placed before anything is stated, so a fall lowers the top she can state and breaks nothing (NUMBERS 8u); restates spine row 4 in Bernstein's frame.
Fri 20 Nov: 3b and 3e: after 2033 only her flexibility, promised to no one, can be forced to sell in a slump by a builder's bill; a slump then a burst is the honest limit (spine row 9, NUMBERS 8q).

Fri 20 Nov: 3e area (4): the case fixes each payment in dollars (l.90) and names other sources for running costs (l.85-86). Fix: quote the case's full list, which includes continued business income and other sources, and say may come from; never that the case hands inflation to the other funders by name.

Fri 20 Nov: 3e area (4), in words: on US prices since 1913 the last payment bought a median of about two-thirds, at worst about a third; a history figure, never a plan figure; Keel arithmetic on FRED, so S 3; the register's 1.9%-3.5% band stays.
Fri 20 Nov: store; Bernstein's funny money and his 25-year safe pot; Laura's ladder is his safe pot for dollar payments, and his inflation-linked ladder is banned and the wrong match (TNA l.7).
Fri 20 Nov: 2.3 or 3a lineage for the order of purchase: Laura wins (owns the ten) before shares get any money; one clause at most beside the order-of-purchase reserve.
Fri 20 Nov: store; France 1940-79, bonds lost 84% real while shares gained 124%: a bondholder paid in full can still be ruined, which l.90 accepts for the ten; as reported in Edesess.

Fri 20 Nov: 3e (idea 4): Bernstein's cures cancel, so the plan gives each to the money it fits, Treasuries for dollar promises and shares for money promised to no one (IPS l.11); pedigree with a point.
Fri 20 Nov: store; stocks do poorly with inflation in the short run, and the building's money has about five years; DMS's -58% is store Q61-028.
Fri 20 Nov: store; the cure works on size and fails on order; mostly restates Q10e-022 and spine row 9; overlapping windows, Keel arithmetic on MSCI ACWI (never VT before 2008).

Fri 20 Nov: store only. Fix: CANON A14 keeps TIPS in the report only as TNA l.7 has them, and Wharton bans them for the Final Report, so never offer inflation-linked Treasuries as a building hedge in 3e; at most say US consumer prices rose 8.1% while the building's dollar cost rose 38.9% (Keel arithmetic).

Fri 20 Nov: 2.3 clause: Bernstein's advice to the young assumes they keep their jobs through the hard times, and IPS l.9's turn is that assumption failing for a writer; human capital itself is pedigree (H9-001).

Fri 20 Nov: 3e two-reasons line (idea 3): of Bernstein's horsemen plus lost income, a default and a missed deposit still reach the payments. Fix: the judges found a missed deposit can be Laura's own act, so never map it only to her income failing or call both exits events outside her control; never only two things can break the plan (CANON A34).
Fri 20 Nov: 3e, deflation helps the promises and hurts the rest (her income, VT, the bottom before January 2028); one clause at most.
Fri 20 Nov: store; EO 6102 took the gold bought against a debased dollar; the plan holds no gold; a fact no part needs.
Fri 20 Nov: twin of H5-041 (Perry: paid in dollars, the risk left is buying power); adds Perry's $16,931.25 claim, the about 41% Keel arithmetic and the dissent; fold them into H5-041.
Fri 20 Nov: 3e, the shares-at-zero test has a historical run: Russia's and China's total losses (DMS 2006); pedigree beside the deletion test, which keeps its own proof sentence.
Fri 20 Nov: store; a world fund shrinks one nation's total loss to its weight (DMS, about 0.1 point; universal Armageddon); survivorship itself is H7-042 and H2-086.
Fri 20 Nov: store; Taiwan and China are 6.1% of VT, about what Russia and China were in 1900; a war would not stay inside those weights; Keel inference, never a forecast.

Fri 20 Nov: 3e limit, in words: devastation can reach the building and the residency's purpose, not money still owed, which waits at a US broker until each 1 January; say Treasuries and Treasury fund shares; the review's line is a paraphrase.
Fri 20 Nov: twin of H6-155 (nominal bonds wiped out by hyperinflation, Japan); Germany's -100% adds a country, not a point; certain as a number, not as a thing is already CONCEIT V2.
Fri 20 Nov: 3c or 3d gloss: a stated figure missed is a deep loss of credibility (case l.114), which is why a figure is stated only once owned (IPS l.15); Keel inference.
Fri 20 Nov: store; a reviewer's critique that the book barely deals with not knowing whether a fall is shallow or deep; a date settles it for Laura; wording summarised, UNVERIFIED.

Fri 20 Nov: 3e, the disanalogy is the point: no longevity risk and no inflation inside the promise, so Laura's deep risks sit in the building, the residency's buying power and her income; Keel synthesis.
Fri 20 Nov: store; Bernstein's probabilities, consequences and costs of mitigation is the shape 3e's recast already has (NUMBERS 8u); a clause of lineage at most.
